about: Eval fixture for the review-layer recall scorer. Incidents are reverts and red-main reverts on main, and merged PRs that a later fix PR found to be a reviewer miss. A revert incident names the PR the revert undid. A fix-found miss names its head and the fix PR (fixed_by) and has no revert. Each incident gives the review layer that should have caught it and a one-line answer key. Controls are merged PRs that no revert names and no fix names as a miss. The layer is the author's judgment from the revert message, the changed files and the PR title. It is not a recorded review verdict. A layer of 'unknown' means the revert gives no cause to judge: the incident stays in the fixture and in n.incidents, and in no layer's count. A layer of 'ci' means CI caught the defect after merge: no review layer replays CI suites, so the incident stays in n.incidents and in no layer's count.
read: 2026-11-17 CST. Reverts from git log on main (subjects and 'This reverts commit' lines). PRs from REST commits/<sha>/pulls or pulls/<n>. Controls from REST pulls/<n>, with commits checked against every reverted commit. 2026-11-18 CST: fix-found misses and their heads from git log on main (a fix PR's merge commit and the miss PR's second parent). Controls added from git log on main merge commits; merged_at is the merge commit's time in UTC, and each title is the PR title on the merge commit. 2026-11-18 CST: PR 3542 relabelled 'ci' (owner pick a: count true reviewer misses only). PR 3596 relabelled 'ci' the same way: its red-main revert is 5e9f66d64d, which names the blamed merge. PR 3628's evidence is its review-log comment on the PR, read from the PR's comments.
